correctness.rationale: For \(q\ge2\), the \(2N-1\) spanning-edge requirement and \((q+1)\)-regularity prove \(|D|\ge2q+1\). The plane incidence axioms imply the exact connectivity criterion: both shore domination conditions plus a selected incidence. At the lower-bound cardinality each shore must have at least \(q\) selected vertices; the \(q\) selected lines must attain their maximal \(q^2+1\)-point union, forcing concurrency, and the other shore is its \(q\) uncovered points plus one covered point. Duality is exhaustive; the extra point has exactly \(q^2+1\) choices, with incidences \(e_D=q\) or \(e_D=1\). The edge-count formula gives cycle rank \(q-e_D\). Two independent standalone \(q\in\{2,3\}\) enumerators constructed from distinct coordinate systems and graph algorithms agree with every computed coefficient; they corroborate but do not replace the all-plane proof.

value.rationale: The exact optimum geometry and count hold uniformly for all finite projective planes (including non-Desarguesian planes) and reveal a natural duality. The sharp edge-count threshold produces a structural, not only numerical, split between \(2N(q+1)\) spanning-star-tree optima and \(2N(q+1)q^2\) connected cyclic optima. The finding gives a complete classifier useful for extremal network-coverage design on highly symmetric incidence networks; it is more informative than a minimum number or a finite table.
